name: Magnetic anomaly detection with an 8-element 77 K HTS SQUID tensor gradiometer cooled by liquid nitrogen
plain_name: Find a hidden metal object from the tiny dent it makes in the Earth's magnetic field using nitrogen-cooled SQUID sensors
description: Passive magnetic anomaly detection (MAD) with Tristan Technologies HTS SQUID systems that use liquid nitrogen (77 K) as refrigerant for cost and portability: the T877 8-element tensor gradiometer was designed specifically for magnetic anomaly measurements; an HTS planar gradiometer in a tail-mounted stinger on a Cessna Caravan recorded the signature of a vehicle; the G377 3-axis 77 K system reaches better than 100 fT/sqrt(Hz).
keywords: Find a hidden metal object from the tiny dent it makes in the Earth's magnetic field using nitrogen-cooled SQUID sensors

sources.citation: Tristan Technologies, General Geophysical Devices (HTS SQUID magnetometer systems)

requirements.rationale: The HTS SQUIDs operate at 77 K.
Eight SQUID gradiometer elements must be biased and read out from the cold space.
Tristan cools these systems with liquid nitrogen for cost and portability; a cryocooler could also reach 77 K, so not mandatory.
